description: Arabic-Indic digits are classified differently by the two engines.
descriptor: { descriptor_version: "1.0", root: { type: "object", children: { a: { type: "string", pattern: "^\\d+$" } } } }

divergence.note: docs/grammars.md §1.2 and §1.3 fix which layer reports each regex construct, and §1.2 states that the two implementations can name the same problem at different layers while the outcome (refused, named, never guessed at) does not differ. This is a documented, intentional divergence from the executed baseline under that rule (SPEC.md amendment 26), not a baseline defect.  docs/grammars.md §1.1 records the measured semantic difference: the shorthand classes are ASCII in this product and Unicode-aware in the baseline engine. The pattern is accepted by both, but Arabic-Indic digits match there and not here. The document fixes the ASCII reading and tells an author who must classify non-ASCII text to state the ranges; the difference is intentional and document-anchored.
